successCriteria.description: The `LeaveBalance` interface is defined in `src/modules/balance/balance.model.ts` with exactly these fields: `id: string`, `employeeId: string`, `leavePolicyId: string`, `totalEntitlement: number`, `usedDays: number`, `remainingDays: number`, `fiscalYear: number`, `status: BalanceStatus`, `createdAt: Date`, `updatedAt: Date`.
The `BalanceStatus` enum is defined in `src/modules/balance/balance.model.ts` with exactly three members: `ACTIVE`, `EXHAUSTED`, `CLOSED`.

The `IBalanceRepository` interface is defined in `src/modules/balance/balance.repository.ts` with all seven methods: `findById`, `findByEmployee`, `findByEmployeeAndPolicy`, `findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear`, `create`, `update`, `delete` — each with the exact signatures specified in PLAN.md Phase 5.

The `IBalanceService` interface is defined in `src/modules/balance/balance.service.interface.ts` with all seven methods: `getById`, `getByEmployee`, `getByEmployeeAndPolicy`, `create`, `deductDays`, `restoreDays`, `hasSufficientBalance` — plus the `CreateBalanceDto` type.

`BalanceService.create` validates that `employeeId` is a non-empty string, `leavePolicyId` is a non-empty string, `totalEntitlement` is a positive finite integer, and `fiscalYear` is a positive integer; rejects invalid input with a `ValidationError` (following the pattern in `LeavePolicyService`).

`BalanceService.deductDays` validates that `days > 0`, the balance exists, its status is `ACTIVE`, and `remainingDays >= days`; on success it increments `usedDays` by `days`, recalculates `remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays`, and transitions status to `EXHAUSTED` when `remainingDays` reaches 0.

`BalanceService.restoreDays` validates that `days > 0`, the balance exists, and `usedDays >= days` (never goes below 0); on success it decrements `usedDays` by `days`, recalculates `remainingDays`, and if status was `EXHAUSTED` and `remainingDays > 0`, reverts status to `ACTIVE`.

`BalanceService.hasSufficientBalance` returns `true` when a balance exists for the given employee+policy and `remainingDays >= requestedDays`; returns `false` when no balance exists or `remainingDays < requestedDays`.

Jest unit tests exist at `tests/unit/modules/balance/balance.service.test.ts` covering: deduction (valid, insufficient balance, non-ACTIVE status, non-existent balance), restoration (valid, would go below zero, EXHAUSTED→ACTIVE transition), sufficiency checks (sufficient, insufficient, missing balance), and status transitions (ACTIVE→EXHAUSTED on zero remaining, EXHAUSTED→ACTIVE on restore). Uses `jest.Mocked<IBalanceRepository>` and a factory function for `LeaveBalance`.

constraints: All database access must go through `IBalanceRepository` — the `BalanceService` must never call the database directly (GP-001).
The `BalanceService` must define its own `ValidationError` class (extending `Error`, setting `name = 'ValidationError'`), following the pattern established by `LeavePolicyService` and `AuditService`.

The `remainingDays` derivation rule is BINDING: `remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays`, computed as an integer (use `Math.floor` if any fractional value arises). This must be recalculated on every mutation of `usedDays` or `totalEntitlement`.
outOfScope: HTTP controllers, routes, and request/response serialization — this phase delivers only the domain model, repository interface, service interface, and service implementation. The balance module has no HTTP surface yet.
Database migrations, Knex schema definitions, and concrete repository implementations (e.g., `BalanceRepository` with PostgreSQL queries) — this phase defines only the `IBalanceRepository` interface.

ambiguities.description: `hasSufficientBalance(employeeId, leavePolicyId, requestedDays)` does not accept a `fiscalYear` parameter. When multiple balances exist for the same employee+policy across different fiscal years, which balance is checked? The natural default is the current calendar year, but the code agent must choose and apply it consistently.
options: Use current calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) as the implicit fiscal year for sufficiency checks
Check all fiscal years and return true if any balance has sufficient remaining days
Require the caller to pass fiscalYear explicitly

entityInvariants.invariant: `remainingDays` is always derived as `totalEntitlement - usedDays` (integer, floored if fractional) and must be recalculated on every mutation of `usedDays` or `totalEntitlement`. It is stored denormalized but must never drift from the derivation.

Lifecycle: `ACTIVE` → `EXHAUSTED` → `CLOSED`. A balance is `ACTIVE` when `remainingDays > 0`. It transitions to `EXHAUSTED` when `remainingDays` reaches 0 after a deduction. It reverts to `ACTIVE` from `EXHAUSTED` when `remainingDays` becomes > 0 after a restoration. `CLOSED` is a terminal state (e.g., fiscal year end) — no deductions or restorations are permitted on a `CLOSED` balance.
`usedDays` must never be negative and must never exceed `totalEntitlement`. `remainingDays` must never be negative.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws `ValidationError` if `days <= 0`, if balance not found, if balance status is not `ACTIVE`, or if `remainingDays < days`. Must never produce a negative `remainingDays`.
Throws `ValidationError` if `days <= 0`, if balance not found, or if `usedDays < days` (cannot restore more than was used). Must never produce a negative `usedDays`.

Returns `false` (never throws) when no balance exists for the given employee+policy combination. Returns `false` when `remainingDays < requestedDays`. Returns `true` only when a balance exists and `remainingDays >= requestedDays`.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `BalanceService` must follow the same module pattern as `LeavePolicyService`: a class with constructor-injected repository, a local `ValidationError` class, input validation before delegation, and barrel export via `index.ts`.

The `LeaveBalance` model's `leavePolicyId` field references `LeavePolicy.id`. The module may import `LeavePolicy` from the policy module's public barrel export (`src/modules/policy/index.ts`) for type-checking, but must never import from policy internals.

The `BalanceService` must use `Math.floor` for the `remainingDays` calculation to match the BINDING rule in the reconciled architecture. This is the same integer-day semantics used throughout the leave management domain.

integrationPoints.why: The balance module does not directly consume shared enums in its model, but the `LeavePolicy` model (which `leavePolicyId` references) imports `LeaveType` from here. The balance module's dependency on shared types is indirect via policy.
